analysis: Only docs/architecture/inference.md changed (date bump, KV re-slice floor note near line 985, a cluster service health-file paragraph near head 3532-3540, and edits around head 5234-5239, 5254-5288, 5295-5298, 5374-5376). The supplied units are base text, lines 4931-5322 and 5323-5376. They cover Qwen media TP, request-owned lanes, native context, cluster media ingress, capability honesty and MTP content. Several head-side hunks (985, 3532, and part of 5254-5288) are not visible in the supplied base text. Where the patch excerpt was cut off, I could not verify its content. This is a documentation-only change with no code, key handling, attestation, or authorization path altered. I found no change that weakens a control in the threat model, or invalidates its assumptions: T-041 (prefix cache; the doc keeps media prefix reuse disabled on this ingress), TB-002, TB-007, T-050 (media plaintext). The base text describes encoded media bytes held only in owner and rank 0 and released after definitive retirement, which is consistent with those mitigations. The new health-file paragraph (DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE, service-health.json versus part-health.json) is described as keeping a supervised part's heartbeat separate from the service's, and the liveness guard accepts only the service's own PID. If the implementation differs, a local process could spoof liveness. The code for it is not in the supplied units, so I cannot verify it. A reviewer of the implementation PR should check the health-file permissions and PID binding (TB-003, T-043 watchdog). Claims about performance and parity are documentation statements, not security controls. No threat-model update is clearly needed from the visible text.
